answer.original_source: NVIDIA Corporation, NVIDIA blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement; sole identified origin of the new-model claim in the supplied records)
answer.new_information: NVIDIA (party statement, 2026-07-01) says a new business model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model. Under the partnership, AI clouds sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services, and NVIDIA earns both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which NVIDIA describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. No dollar amounts, percentages, credit-support size or term, signing status, counterparties beyond the named partners, or effective period are given. Named partner statements in the same record (item:e2 Sharon AI CEO; item:e3 NVIDIA on DSX AI factories being built across regions; item:e4 NVIDIA on Firmus Batam, Indonesia campus expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) are forward-looking plans or party descriptions, not confirmed deployments, orders or revenue for NVDA. Inference: if the credit support is a guarantee or financing commitment by NVIDIA, it would be an obligation whose size is currently unknown; if the revenue share is real, it may affect the mix and recurrence of NVDA revenue, but that is not quantified in the supplied text. Customer backlog, AI cloud revenue and Firmus capacity are not NVDA revenue or orders.
answer.reason: No catalog question or stored piece exists, so this is a distinct investment judgement that no catalog question carries. It qualifies under the financing/guarantee/purchase-obligation admission reason because NVIDIA's credit-support element may create a guarantee or financing commitment whose terms are unspecified and unsigned. Public evidence that will settle it: NVIDIA's annual 10-K for fiscal 2027 (filed around February 2027) and any subsequent 10-Q disclosures of guarantees, credit support, revenue-share arrangements or receivables, plus named signed partner agreements. Check date: next annual filing (FY2027 10-K), which falls within 18 months of 2026-07-01 for the unsigned-obligation signing check. Nearest catalog question: none exists in the empty catalog. Folding into an existing question would lose the distinct question of whether NVDA takes on guarantee or financing exposure and whether its revenue mix shifts toward usage-linked cloud revenue.

arguments.statement: Lean: unresolved, with a modest tilt toward NVDA taking on new credit-support and revenue-share economics with AI clouds. The incoming NVIDIA statement supports that NVIDIA has announced a model with revenue sharing and credit support and expects both product revenue and a share of cloud revenue. The partner statements (item:e2, item:e3, item:e4) support only that AI cloud partners are building DSX AI factories, with Firmus expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs. None of the supplied records state the size, term, signing status or accounting of the credit support, so the financial magnitude to NVDA cannot be assessed.
limitations: Sole origin is NVIDIA's own blog post; no independent confirmation of terms or amounts is in the supplied records.
Credit-support and revenue-share terms are unspecified; no amount, percentage, period or counterparty list beyond named partners.
Firmus capacity figures are expected/plan figures and are not confirmed deployments or NVDA orders.
Partner quotes are party statements relayed by NVIDIA.
No stored pieces or prior catalog questions exist to compare against.
what_would_change_it: NVIDIA 10-K or 10-Q disclosure of guarantees, credit support, or revenue-share receivables tied to AI cloud partners, with amounts and periods.
Signed agreements with named AI cloud partners specifying credit-support amounts, terms and revenue-share percentages.
Evidence that Firmus or other partners have reached financing close or deployed the stated GPU capacity.
Any NVIDIA statement quantifying the expected share of revenue from cloud partners in a given fiscal year.

answer.independent_judgement: The incoming record is a single-origin party statement describing a new commercial model. It is a distinct judgement worth tracking because it may introduce guarantee-like credit support and a usage-linked revenue stream for NVDA. Current evidence does not establish any amount, obligation or revenue effect, so the investment direction stays unresolved pending the annual filing and signed agreements.
answer.new_question: Will NVIDIA's fiscal 2027 annual filing or subsequent disclosures show material credit-support, guarantee or revenue-share obligations to AI cloud partners under the new model, and what share of NVDA revenue will come from cloud-linked revenue-sharing?
